what: The always-current internal site: a reusable generator, in its own repository and consumed as a versioned Action, that turns this repository's own records and GitHub issues into a milestone depth chart, a phone triage view, and the records themselves
position:
Eight milestones done, through Atlas v1.5.0. M1 built the generator; M2 adopted it here and put atlas.vennusign.com live behind an invited role; M2.1 rebuilt the feature planning page as drawn paths and made it reorderable; M3 shipped write-back as two managed Functions; M4 was the drawn page's second pass plus a live-feedback round (theme picker, header styling, wrap fix, divergent milestone labels). M4.1 — unplanned, the way M2.1 was — then retired the drawn chart entirely for an accordion + milestone spine, with task checklists parsed from each milestone's own GitHub issue: a lightweight version of an idea M6 already had a fuller design for (native sub-issues, `agent:<name>` labels, a task-row grid), built instead as inline checkboxes with a trailing owner tag because that is what the owner asked for in the moment. M6 is not superseded by this — it is now the open question of whether to reconcile the two, and how. M7 (a local scaffold CLI for onboarding a new feature onto this sheet) and M8 (real deployment stages, replacing the old "shipping" vocabulary — this field's own value included) shipped next.

M7 and M8 were both given fresh top-level numbers while M5 and M6 — already fully planned, M5 with a complete 6-task plan on record — sat untouched. That was a real process lapse, caught by the owner from the live site rather than caught here first: a milestone number should not leapfrog an already-planned, unstarted one without a stated reason, and when it does for a stated reason, it should be a sub-milestone of the current active thread (M4.1's own pattern), not a fresh top-level slot. M7/M8 are not renumbered after the fact — decision 17 treats milestone ids as durable once shipped, referenced in commits and PR history — but the rule now governs anything after them. M5 and M6 remain the next real work, in that order, unless a stated reason says otherwise.
gate: Write-back is live and verified (a GitHub App with contents-write on this repo) and, as of M8, covers three things — a register answer, an acceptance result, and a deployment-transition record — not two. Nothing new blocks M5 or M6. #780's original findings on the feature planning page are superseded by `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-feature-planning-rebuild-design.md` in the Atlas repo (M4.1's spec), which is now the authoritative record for that page; #780 itself was left open on GitHub rather than closed unilaterally. M6 specifically still needs a decision before its plan can proceed unmodified: reconcile it with what M4.1 already shipped (inline checklists, an open owner-tag vocabulary), supersede M4.1's approach with M6's fuller one, or explicitly keep both and say why. Separately, decision 32's milestone-status vocabulary (`done, next, blocked, parked, unplanned`) has no word for "fully planned, not yet started" — M5 already has a complete plan on record and is still labelled `unplanned` for lack of a better closed value; a real gap, not yet fixed, surfaced by this same review.
